tools.description: Show a protein, or a complex of proteins, DNA, RNA and small-molecule ligands, in an interactive 3D viewer from sequences. Use it when the user wants to see or visualize a structure or how molecules fit together, such as a protein bound to ATP, a protein on DNA, or a homodimer, or when you need to look at one to answer a question about its shape. Give one entity per distinct molecule, in order, with copies for identical chains; give each DNA strand as its own entity; a ligand takes a CCD code or a SMILES string, such as [{"type": "protein", "sequence": "MKTAYIAKQR"}, {"type": "ligand", "ccd": "ATP"}]. For a protein name or accession, get the sequence first with esm_atlas_search_uniprot or esm_atlas_lookup_accession. One protein with one copy returns its ESM Atlas structure when one exists, or a prediction for up to 700 residues, at no cost. Anything else is a new fold with ESMFold2 on the Biohub Platform billed to the signed-in user's Biohub account, so call it once per request; a complex holds up to 768 tokens, one per residue or nucleotide and one per ligand heavy atom, counted for every copy, in at most 36 chains; larger complexes need the Batch API. Structures are computational predictions, not experimental. In clients that support MCP Apps, the user gets an interactive viewer they can rotate, recolor, and select residues in without another call; the result has each entity's chain IDs, pTM, ipTM and warnings, and only the viewer gets the coordinates. Nothing is saved and no link is created. The result has no image by default. Set include_png to true only when you need to see the structure yourself or the client can't show the viewer, because it adds several seconds. Without an image, don't describe how the structure looks.

tools.description: Look up what the ESM Atlas knows about one protein sequence: its source accession, the confidence of its predicted structure (pTM and mean pLDDT), whether a structure exists or can be predicted (up to 700 residues), and its strongest ESMC sparse-autoencoder (SAE) features, which are learned, labeled protein properties, with the residue ranges that drive them. Use it first for a sequence you already have. Takes a raw one-letter sequence; resolve a protein name or accession with esm_atlas_search_uniprot or esm_atlas_lookup_accession. Sequences not in the ESM Atlas get features computed for up to 2,048 residues. This tool never predicts a structure; ui_show_structure with the same sequence shows one. No saved ID or download is created.

tools.description: Find ESM Atlas protein clusters whose representatives are most similar to a sequence, compared by ESMC sparse-autoencoder (SAE) feature profiles rather than by sequence alignment. Use it to find functional or structural neighbors of a protein. Takes a raw one-letter sequence up to 2,048 residues. Returns up to top_k representatives above a minimum similarity, so fewer may come back, each with a similarity score, cluster size, name, and a sequence to pass to the other ESM Atlas tools, plus the features most shared across hits. restricted_count is the number of hits withheld by safety screening. Hits without a stored structure may be predicted during the search, which can add time.

tools.description: Get the ESM Atlas cluster a protein belongs to: cluster size, the share of members with characterized Pfam annotations, top Pfam domains, taxonomy and top phyla, and the SAE features typical of the cluster. ESM Atlas clusters group proteins by ESMC sparse-autoencoder (SAE) feature similarity, not by sequence identity. Use it to put a protein in context or judge how well studied its neighborhood is. Takes the raw one-letter sequence of a protein already in the ESM Atlas, such as a hit from esm_atlas_search_similar_protein_clusters; other sequences return not_found, because this tool computes nothing.

tools.description: Predict structure confidence with ESMFold2 for one protein, several protein chains (an antibody, a homodimer, a binder and its target), or proteins with DNA, RNA or ligands. It returns scores on a 0-to-1 scale: pTM, a pLDDT summary, interface pTM for the whole complex, and ipTM per chain pair when returned. Protein folds can also return mean pLDDT per chain; a warning says when it is unavailable. A high pTM with a low interface pTM means each part is confident alone but the contact is not. These are predictions, not measured binding. It never returns a structure or coordinates. For free, esm_atlas_get_protein_details gives the ESM Atlas pTM and mean pLDDT of a protein already in the Atlas, and ui_show_structure shows one protein chain with a single protein entity, predicting it if needed for up to 700 residues. Inputs of up to 768 tokens fold within the call and return done. Longer inputs, up to 4,096, or use_batch_api=true, return queued with a run_id at one fifth of the price, readable with biohub_get_inference_run for 31 days. It takes no alignment; esmfold2_fold_max_accuracy builds one. It bills the signed-in user's Biohub account, growing with the square of the length: about 0.45 credits for 300 residues within the call and 4 for 2,000 as a run. Each call starts new work and can bill again; an indeterminate failure may already have been billed.

Up to 4,096 tokens: one per residue or nucleotide, one per ligand heavy atom. An input Biohub routes at 768 tokens or fewer but the worker counts above that limit is refused before anything is submitted.

tools.description: Predict structure confidence at Biohub's highest accuracy, slower and costlier than esmfold2_fold_complex, for the same entities. Biohub builds its own alignment from UniRef30 and ColabFold, and the tool cannot take one; it folds five times with different seeds and keeps the most confident. It always returns queued with a run_id, readable with biohub_get_inference_run for 31 days; a run takes minutes to hours. Its scores, on a 0-to-1 scale, are pTM, a pLDDT summary, interface pTM and ipTM per chain pair when returned. It does not return per-chain pLDDT. It never returns a structure or coordinates. It bills the signed-in user's Biohub account when the run finishes, with no batch discount: about 0.28 credits for 56 residues, 1.6 for 300, 4.4 for 768, 14 for 2,000 and 37 for 4,096. By default the signed-in user's Biohub account can start 10 of these runs a day, and a run that fails is not charged but still counts. Each call starts new work and can bill again; an indeterminate failure may already have been billed.

tools.description: Score substitutions the user already named, such as W43F or a list from a paper, in one protein with ESMC. Each is scored alone on the wild-type sequence, not as part of a combined variant. The score is ln P(substituted) - ln P(wild type) with that position masked, so a positive score means ESMC finds the new residue more likely there. These are predictions, not measured fitness, stability or activity. It bills the signed-in user's Biohub account one ESMC call per distinct position, at most 8, each costing the protein's length divided by 10,000 credits, so any substitutions at 3 positions of a 300-residue protein cost 0.09 credits. Each call starts new work and can bill again; an indeterminate failure may already have been billed. esmc_scan_mutation_tolerance finds positions worth testing when none are named.

sequence.description: One protein chain of 1 to 2,046 residues in one-letter codes; whitespace is ignored, and '|' and ':' are refused.

tools.description: Find where a protein is most and least tolerant to change, when no substitutions are named yet. It masks each scanned position, scores all 20 amino acids with ESMC, and returns only the most constrained and most tolerant positions, ranked by ranking_metric, with their strongest substitutions, not the full matrix. These are predictions, not measured fitness. It bills the signed-in user's Biohub account one ESMC call per scanned position, so a scan costs positions times length divided by 10,000 credits: 9 for all of a 300-residue protein, and never more than 20. Each call starts new work and can bill again; an indeterminate failure may already have been billed. At the time limit, or on a rate limit after some positions finished, it stops starting calls and returns partial, billed for the finished positions only, with the rest in coverage.unscanned. Otherwise a failure returns an error, and positions that finished were still billed. It never shortens a long protein silently, and offers the 300M, 600M and 6B models.

sequence.description: One protein chain of 1 to 2,046 residues in one-letter codes; whitespace is ignored, and '|' and ':' are refused.

anyOf.description: A 1-based window of positions, both ends included.

positions.description: "all", a list of 1-based positions, or {start, end}. At most 400 positions, and fewer for long proteins: 200,000 divided by the length. Over that, the tool refuses with a window to try; it never shortens the scan.

model_id.description: esmc-600m-2024-12 has about 600 million parameters and 36 layers; esmc-300m-2024-12 has about 300 million parameters and 30 layers; esmc-6b-2024-12, the default, has about 6 billion parameters and 80 layers; all cost the same per call.

ranking_metric.description: entropy_bits, the default, ranks by entropy in bits over ESMC's full output vocabulary at the masked position, every column of the row and not only the 20 amino acids; low means constrained. negative_substitution_fraction ranks by the share of the 19 other amino acids that score below the wild type, high meaning constrained, with ties broken by entropy.
